name: Deep Water Culture (DWC)
description: Plant roots hang directly into an oxygenated nutrient solution reservoir, suspended by net pots in a floating platform.
advantages: Fast growth due to constant nutrient/oxygen access
Low mechanical complexity — fewer moving parts to fail
Excellent for leafy greens and herbs at scale
limitations: Requires a reliable air pump — root suffocation risk on power outage
Less suited to large, heavy fruiting plants without extra support
Water temperature stability is critical to prevent root rot

name: Nutrient Film Technique (NFT)
description: A thin, continuously flowing film of nutrient solution runs along sloped channels over exposed plant roots.
advantages: Very water and nutrient efficient — solution is recirculated
Good root oxygenation from thin film exposure
Scales well for commercial leafy green production
limitations: Highly vulnerable to pump failure — roots dry out within minutes
Not ideal for large root systems or heavy fruiting crops
Channel clogging can starve downstream plants

name: Ebb and Flow
description: Also called flood and drain — a grow tray is periodically flooded with nutrient solution, then drained back to a reservoir.
advantages: Flexible for many crop types and container/media setups
Good balance of oxygen and nutrient delivery via flood cycles
Tolerant of brief pump interruptions since media retains moisture
limitations: Requires reliable timers to avoid over/under-watering
Growing media can build up salts over time, needs flushing
Moderate complexity to balance flood duration and frequency

name: Drip System
description: Nutrient solution is delivered directly to the base of each plant through drip emitters, either recovery or non-recovery.
advantages: Well suited to larger fruiting crops with high water demand
Easy to scale from small to large commercial operations
limitations: Emitters can clog and require regular maintenance
Non-recovery systems waste runoff unless captured and reused
Slightly more plumbing complexity than reservoir-based systems

name: Aeroponics
description: Roots are suspended in air inside a chamber and misted with nutrient solution at short intervals for maximum oxygenation.
advantages: Highest oxygenation of any method — very fast growth potential
Low disease pressure with well-managed misting cycles
limitations: Very sensitive to pump/nozzle failure — roots desiccate within minutes
Nozzle clogging requires frequent cleaning and filtration
Highest technical complexity and cost of setup

name: Vertical Farming
description: Stacked growing layers (often combined with NFT, DWC, or ebb-and-flow) maximize yield per square meter of floor space using LED lighting.
advantages: Maximizes production density in limited floor space
Enables full climate and light control, independent of outdoor weather
Well suited to urban farms and controlled-environment agriculture
limitations: High upfront investment in racking, lighting, and climate control
Higher energy consumption due to full-spectrum LED lighting
Not practical for tall or heavy fruiting crops
